findings.source: Peace Palace Library (The Hague) — WorldCat Discovery (peacepalace.on.worldcat.org)
findings.captured: HAR of a live browser session, 2026-09-02 (Edge/Chromium, sanitized export: no Cookie/Set-Cookie/Authorization headers), advanced search with two result pages

access.auth: UNCERTAIN. Every SPA request carries three headers: Oclc-Apik (64 hex chars) and Oclc-Apin (40 decimal digits) — BOTH DIFFERENT ON EVERY REQUEST (42 distinct pairs in 42 requests), i.e. a per-request signature computed in the SPA bundle; and api-token, a JWE (header {"cty":"jwt","enc":"A256CBC-HS512","alg":"dir"}) constant across the two /api/search calls, i.e. a session token. Their origin is not in the capture (no page-load entry). The server sends unsigned requests; the probe canary 'worldcat' reports whether they are served. The site sits behind Cloudflare (CF-RAY FRA).
access.detail:
SEARCH (verbatim, entries 0 and 42): GET /api/search?queryString=<q>&databaseList=10007,10025,10052,10058,10306,10896,11162,11537,2795,3313,3560,3577,3578,3583,3590,3962,3963,4023,4052,4056,638&sortKey=BEST_MATCH&clusterResults=true&groupVariantRecords=false&bookReviews=off&year=2021..2025&content=fullText&idDetect=true&citeDetect=true[&page=2]. Request headers: Accept: application/json, text/plain, */*; Accept-Language: en; Referer: the /search?… page with the same parameters.
queryString is WorldCat's index syntax as the advanced form composes it: kw:(keword) AND ti:(title) OR au:(author) — index labels kw/ti/au/su; the backend's echoed queryOptimization.originalQuery shows the `year` parameter rewritten into `( (yr:2021..2025) )`. la:<marc code> is the documented language index (not in the capture). `content=fullText` = the 'Full Text' content facet (other facet values seen: openAccess, peerReviewed, notFic).
RESPONSE: {databaseList[], locale, numberOfRecords (12279), parsedQuery[{field,text,boolean,start,end}], partialResult (bool), providerSearchRequest (an internal SRU 'worldcat-plus' URL — the engine is SRU/CQL), queryExpansion{}, queryOptimization{originalQuery,…}, records[10], searchResultsType: NORMAL}. Page size is fixed at 10; page 2 = records 11–20.
RECORD fields seen (books only — the captured query matched no articles): oclcNumber, titleObject{data}, authors[{firstNameObject{data}, lastNameObject{data}, primary, type, relatorList}], date, publishers[{data}], itemType (book_digital), itemTypeDisplay (eBook), language (eng), isbns[], digitalObjectIdentifiers[], summariesObjectList[{data}], contentsObjects[{note, noteObject{data}}], subjectGroups[{bibSubjects[{data, unifiedData{displayData}, thesaurusType, type}], id, label}], physicalDescription, edition, editionOclcNumbers[], workId, links[{url,label?,accessMethod}], opacLink (a /search?queryString=no:<oclc> or ib:<isbn> deep link), peerReviewed, openAccess, remoteDatabase, databaseId ('' for WorldCat.org), sourceCollection (xwc), genres[], seriesSeparatedFieldsList[], heldByInstitutionName, staffILLRequestUrl, highlightedRecord (a copy for UI highlighting, dropped from the fixtures).
Record permalink used: https://peacepalace.on.worldcat.org/oclc/<oclcNumber>.

access.detail: Same query parameters as /api/search (clusterResults=false). facets.facetGroups keyed by name; values seen: scope (wz:45289 = Peace Palace Library, zs:34227 = Netherlands), format (Book → book_digital; Artchap → artchap_artcl, artchap_digital), content (bio, fic, fullText, notFic, openAccess, peerReviewed), topic (Conspectus codes), year (2021..2025), author, database (Z-wcorg WorldCat.org 9103, Nomos_el 3231, Cup_journals 35, Boom_juri, Bp_bc, Brill_bps_hrhl, Brill_cwto, Brill_hwgdso, Brill_ieclo, Brill_ilwo, Brill_imbo, Brill_rlpic, Brill_uncls, Dh_dhej, Eee_eel, Eee_epil, Eep_eo, Kluwer_kloj, Oup_ouplc, Springerlink), language (Eng, Ger, Spa, Fre…), materialtype. The URL parameters that apply format/language/database facets were NOT captured — hence no format filter in the tool.

Per-record access links (elink: ELinksResponse.result[{id, links[{links[{url, provider, collection, title, openAccess}], type: Primary/Secondary}], doiLinks}]), holdings/editions (localeditions[{localEditions[{oclcNum, titleObject, bibAuthors, date, publisherObjectList, heldLocally, numberOfHoldings}]}]) and usage stats. Not used by the tool; the links[] on the search record cover the access-link need.

access.auth: SimpleSAMLphp IdP of the library (AuthState → spentityid=https://shib.oclc.org/shibboleth): OCLC's Shibboleth SP, i.e. WorldCat Discovery sign-in via the library's own IdP with a username and password
access.detail: Only the login-page URL is known (user-supplied). Not captured: the entry point on peacepalace.on.worldcat.org that starts the SAML dance, the redirect chain through shib.oclc.org back to the Discovery session, and which cookies carry the signed-in state. What signing in changes for SEARCH is also unknown — possibly nothing for WorldCat.org records, possibly access to the licensed databases in databaseList.

unverified: la:<code> as the language index inside queryString (documented WorldCat index label; not in the capture).
Article records' field names (journal title, volume, pages) — the capture holds books only.
page=1 explicitly (the SPA omits the parameter on the first page; the client mirrors that).
needs_from_user: A HAR that INCLUDES the initial page load of https://peacepalace.on.worldcat.org/search?queryString=… (document request + the JS bundles it loads) — to locate where api-token comes from and how Oclc-Apik/Oclc-Apin are computed; a HAR of an article-heavy search (e.g. a Kluwer journal topic) for the article record shape; a HAR of the sign-in flow from the 'Sign in' link through peacepalacelibrary.nl back to the results page, exported WITH cookies but with the password POST removed or redacted.
findings.live_2026_09_02: From the production deployment (fra1, IP 3.125.160.75): GET /api/search unsigned → HTTP 403 in ~50 ms with Cloudflare's 'Sorry, you have been blocked' page (Ray ID a34ba4d969938ff2) — a WAF block of the deployment's request before any OCLC code runs, so the signing headers are moot from this address. The status page shows the library red with HTTP 403; doctrine_search reports the refusal per call. Ways forward are the operator's call: OCLC's official WorldCat Search API with a WSKey issued through the library, or dropping the client as with ÚPV.

findings.source: Univerzita Karlova — UKAŽ, Primo VE (cuni.primo.exlibrisgroup.com, vid 420CKIS_INST:UKAZ)
findings.captured: HAR of a live browser session, 2026-09-02 (sanitized export), one advanced search that matched nothing; a second HAR of the start of the CAS login (idp.cuni.cz → cas.cuni.cz login form, no credentials posted)

access.auth: UNCERTAIN. The pnxs request in the capture shows no Authorization header, but the sanitized export strips that header, and Primo VE's SPA normally sends a guest JWT. The client calls without one and, on 401/403, asks GET /primaws/rest/pub/institution/420CKIS_INST/jwt?isGuest=true&lang=cs&targetUrl=…&viewId=420CKIS_INST:UKAZ (from memory of the SPA, not from the capture) and retries with Authorization: Bearer <jwt>. No cookies are needed for the captured call.

access.auth: Primo → Shibboleth IdP idp.cuni.cz (SAML2 Redirect SSO, entityId of the SP https://cuni.primo.exlibrisgroup.com/mng/login) → external authn → CAS (cas.cuni.cz). CAS form (captured): POST /cas/login?service=<idp callback> with username, password, execution (a long JWT-like flow token from the page), _eventId=submit; an alternative e-Identity (NIA) button.
access.detail: Captured only up to the CAS login page. Not captured: the CAS ticket redirect back to idp.cuni.cz, the SAMLResponse POST to Primo/Alma (/mng/login), and how the signed-in state reaches the SPA (a user JWT). What signing in changes for SEARCH is unknown — Primo's guest search already covers the UK catalogue and the Central Discovery Index; the login matters for full-text access through the university's proxy, which is not a search concern.

unverified: dr_e as YYYY1231 for the 'to' year (the capture shows dr_s=20250101, dr_e=20260101 for the user's range; the tool writes an inclusive year end).
The guest-JWT endpoint (never needed so far — pnxs answers without a token).
needs_from_user: A HAR of the same advanced search with a query that DOES match (e.g. 'genocida', 10 hits), exported WITH sensitive data (so the Authorization header and any jwt call are visible; do it logged out, as a guest, so no personal session is in it) — this pins both the auth question and the real record shape and lets the synthetic fixture be replaced by a verbatim one.

If the reader login is wanted: a HAR of the whole login (Primo 'Přihlásit' → idp.cuni.cz → cas.cuni.cz → back to Primo), with the password POST removed or redacted, plus a statement of what the login is expected to change for the search.
findings.live_2026_09_02: From the production deployment: pnxs answers HTTP 200 WITHOUT any Authorization header (canary and three searches); 'genocida' = 443 local + 10 346 Central Discovery Index records; the full-display endpoint GET /primaws/rest/pub/pnxs/L/alma990020025980106986?vid=…&lang=cs&search_scope=MyInst_and_CI answers 200 with the full record and holdings. Verbatim responses kept as fixtures (search-cdi-article.json, search-local-book.json, record-local-book.json). Seen in the records: display.contents (table of contents of catalogue books), display.identifier as '$$CISBN$$V…' or 'DOI: …'/'ISSN: …', display.oa ['free_for_read'], delivery.link thumbnails with RELATIVE linkURLs ('api/image/…'), pnx.links openurl/openurlfulltext as '$$T…' templates (no URL), delivery.availability ['fulltext'] / ['available_in_library'].

findings.source: Full texts — Unpaywall (api.unpaywall.org) + DOI resolver (doi.org) + publisher/repository copies
findings.captured: Unpaywall: 12 verbatim responses inside the WorldCat HAR (the Discovery SPA asks api.unpaywall.org/v2/<doi>?email=worldcatpm@oclc.org for every DOI it lists) — three kept as fixtures (bronze with PDF, gold with landing page only, closed).

access.auth: none — a contact e-mail per request is the only requirement (UNPAYWALL_EMAIL, default = the operator's public contact)
access.detail: RESPONSE (verbatim fields): doi, doi_url, is_oa, oa_status (gold|hybrid|bronze|green|closed), best_oa_location{url, url_for_pdf, url_for_landing_page, license, version, host_type, repository_institution}, oa_locations[…same…], first_oa_location, genre, title, journal_name, journal_issns, year, published_date, has_repository_copy. 404 for an unknown DOI.

access.base_url: https://doi.org/{doi} and whatever Unpaywall or the catalogue record links to
access.auth: none for open-access copies; licensed copies answer with a login/purchase page or 401/403, which the client reports as 'unavailable' (never as the work)
access.detail: GET with Accept: application/pdf, text/html; redirects followed by hand (max 5) and EVERY hop checked: https only, real hostname, all resolved addresses public (no RFC 1918, loopback, link-local, CGNAT, ULA). PDF (Content-Type or %PDF magic) → unpdf extractText mergePages; HTML → htmlToText, rejected as a wall when under 2 500 characters or when a short page speaks of sign-in/purchase/institutional access. 12 MB body cap (streamed), 20 s per copy, ≤ 3 open + 2 reader copies, 45 s total from the start of the call, PDFs over 1 500 pages refused; HTML decoded by its declared charset; when Unpaywall says closed, any sign-in/purchase vocabulary on an open landing page counts as a wall whatever its length; text cached 10 min per URL (per reader for proxied copies).

unverified: Live behaviour of doi.org and publisher hosts from the deployment (no egress from the development sandbox); the extraction path is pinned by a generated two-page PDF and synthetic HTML.

Primo VE full-display endpoint GET /primaws/rest/pub/pnxs/{L|PC}/{recordid}?vid=…&lang=cs&search_scope=MyInst_and_CI (from memory; the capture never opened a record) — a miss is reported, and the search result already carries the record's main fields.

Residual risk, accepted: the public-address guard resolves the host once and fetch() resolves it again — a DNS-rebinding host (TTL 0, two answers) could pass the check and then hand the connection to a private address. Pinning the socket to the checked address needs a custom undici dispatcher (a new dependency); the deployment's function network has no sensitive peers, so the guard is kept as is and this is recorded rather than papered over.
needs_from_user: Nothing for the open-access path beyond a deploy + dawmain_probe_sources (canary 'unpaywall'). For licensed works: the reader-login captures listed above, and the decision whether readers' library passwords may be stored at all.
findings.live_2026_09_02: From the production deployment: api.unpaywall.org/v2/<doi>?email=… did not answer within 12 s on three tries around 09:56 UTC (timeout, no HTTP status), then answered HTTP 200 in 322 ms at 10:04 UTC — a transient outage or throttle, not a block. The tool waits at most 6 s for it and tries the DOI and the record's links regardless.

findings.source: Reader login through the libraries' proxies — EZproxy + IdP (SimpleSAMLphp / Shibboleth→CAS)
findings.captured: Peace Palace: the proxy host peacepalace.idm.oclc.org/login?url=… (in every licensed access link the Discovery SPA builds) and the IdP login-page URL peacepalacelibrary.nl/saml/module.php/core/loginuserpass?AuthState=… (spentityid=https://shib.oclc.org/shibboleth) supplied by the user. UK: the start of the Primo login (idp.cuni.cz SAML2 Redirect → idp.cuni.cz/idp/Authn/External → cas.cuni.cz/cas/login?service=…) and the CAS login page with its two forms (fm1: username, password, hidden execution + _eventId=submit + geolocation; formNIA: e-Identity) — tests/fixtures/cas-login-form.html.

access.auth: the reader's own library username/password, stored sealed on /ucet
access.detail: No chain is hard-coded. The walker follows redirects with a per-domain cookie jar, fills the first form that has a password input (all hidden fields included — CAS execution/_eventId, SimpleSAMLphp AuthState), auto-posts a form carrying SAMLResponse, and stops at the first page that is neither (the work, or a wall). A password form seen twice = refused login (SESSION_EXPIRED). Every hop passes the public-address guard. One proxy session (cookie jar) per reader and library, 30 min, on a warm instance. Guards: the credential is posted only to a password form whose page AND action live on the library's own sign-in hosts by exact hostname and default port (cuni: the proxy host, cas.cuni.cz, idp.cuni.cz; peacepalace: peacepalace.idm.oclc.org, shib.oclc.org, *.peacepalacelibrary.nl) — never a suffix, because EZproxy serves the publisher from a rewritten subdomain of the proxy host and that page is the publisher's, sign-in widget included — a password box anywhere else is not a login and the page is returned as content; a refused login (the form shown again after the POST) is remembered per reader+library+credential for 30 minutes and not replayed; Set-Cookie Domain attributes are honoured only for the responder's own domain (RFC 6265 §5.3); bodies are read with a streamed 12 MB cap; hidden-only forms carrying an SSO hand-off field (SAMLResponse/SAMLRequest/RelayState/wa/wresult/wctx/_eventId…) are auto-posted at most 5 times per walk and only while on the sign-in hosts, with the first named submit button included; GET forms are submitted as GET. The chain must end on the proxy's host or the target's host; anywhere else (a consent page, an institution picker) is reported as an interstitial the walker does not know.

unverified: The whole redirect chain of both libraries (never captured end to end): whether EZproxy hands off to the IdP as expected, whether the IdP's SAMLResponse page is a plain auto-post form (a JavaScript-only page or a second factor would stop the walker), and the UK proxy hostname.
Whether the libraries' proxies accept a datacenter IP (fra1) at all.
needs_from_user: After deploy: store a login on /ucet, call doctrine_get_document on a licensed hit and read access.tried — each hop's outcome names what did not fit. If a chain stops, a HAR of the same sign-in in a browser (password POST removed) pins the missing step.

decisions: One tool, doctrine_search, fans out to both catalogues (the cz_caselaw_search shape): same criteria, per-source status, per-source totals and has_more, grouped output.

Both catalogues serve fixed pages of 10; per_source_limit (≤ 20; above 10 records come brief, without abstract/contents, to stay inside the response budget) is served by fetching the covering catalogue pages in a parallel batch, page walks further (pageWindow/sliceWindow in src/sources/shared/bib.ts).
No sort/format filters: their URL parameters were not captured and a guessed one would silently answer a different question.

Reading a work = doctrine_get_document: the record in full first (orientation is possible without any copy), then the first readable copy from an ordered candidate list, every failed copy reported with its reason. Open copies first (Unpaywall, DOI, record links); then, for an OAuth-identified caller with a login stored on /ucet, the same works through that library's proxy — access.status distinguishes open from reader.

Readers' library logins live sealed (AES-256-GCM, CREDENTIALS_SECRET) in Clerk private metadata and are used only for the OAuth-identified caller; the shared access code cannot use them. The privacy policy names the new data category.

Reader login is automated as a browser-like walk (src/sources/library-login.ts), not a hard-coded chain: no library's entry point and redirect chain is captured end to end, so the walker follows what the server sends and reports the hop that did not fit. Storing readers' library passwords was taken as the operator's decision (asked for twice); the privacy policy names the category.
